text.p: Norwegian metals producer Elkem ASA is expected to show a 13 percent dip in full-year 1996 pre-tax profits, a Reuter poll of nine analysts showed.
The average estimate indicated pre-tax profits at 940 million crowns compared with a 1995 profit of 1.08 billion crowns.
Five of the analysts recommended selling the stock, two said hold and two said buy.

The analysts said the focus on the company had shifted from the demand and price of metals to money market rates and the Norwegian power market, both of which had developed negatively for Elkem's business.

Power prices were at record high levels throughout 1996 due to low water levels in Norway's hydropower reservoirs. In addition, a rally in the Norwegian crown at the beginning of 1997 has sent it to 52-month highs against the German mark.
"Exchange rates can have an enormous impact in the short term," said one trader, who was pessimistic on the company in the case that the crown continued to strengthen.
Others said that in the longer-term, gains made on foreign exchange borrowings and lower prices for imported goods for Elkem's production would dampen the effect of the crown.

"The worst case would be a five to 10 percent reduction in earnings per share (EPS) estimates for 1998. But Elkem won't want to sit still and watch that happen. Therefore we may see some cost cuts," said another analyst.
Elkem will release full-year 1996 results on February 11.
